en: The human jaw acts as a third-class lever when you bite food with your front teeth.
Geckos climb smooth glass because millions of microscopic hairs on their feet use molecular attraction, not sticky secretions.
The gravitational pull of the Moon is so weak that a 100-pound child would weigh only 17 pounds there.
Heating a permanent magnet to a high enough temperature completely scrambles its aligned atoms, destroying its magnetism.
A single bolt of lightning contains enough energy to toast roughly 100,000 slices of bread.
Sunlight takes exactly eight minutes and twenty seconds to travel the 150 million kilometers from the Sun to Earth.
The loudest natural sound ever recorded on Earth was the 1883 eruption of Krakatoa, heard 3,000 miles away.
You can make water simultaneously boil and freeze at a specific temperature and pressure known as its triple point.
A roller coaster momentarily stops at the very top of its highest hill, converting all its kinetic energy into maximum potential energy.
A single fixed pulley changes the direction of your pulling force but provides absolutely zero mechanical advantage.
The intense heat generated by air friction is what causes most small meteors to burn up before hitting Earth.
A static electricity spark from your finger can reach 3,000 volts, though it lacks the current to harm you.
